A 64-year-old male presents to the emergency department with rectal bleeding, crampy abdominal
pain, recent weight loss, and fever. He also reports blood in his urine. His vital signs include a blood
pressure of 140/98 mmHg, pulse of 72 bpm, and respiratory rate of 18/min. He states that his blood
pressure has never been this high before (previously recorded as 120/70 mmHg two months ago).
Physical examination reveals abdominal tenderness and cutaneous ischemic ulcers. **Renal Function

Test:** - Blood urea nitrogen: 90 mg/dL - Serum creatinine: 2.5 mg/dL - Serum uric acid: 4.7 mg/dL -
Serum calcium: 8.66 mg/dL - Serum sodium: 150 mEq/L - Serum potassium: 5.00 mEq/L - Serum
chloride: 107.7 mEq/L Additional labs show elevated ESR and C-reactive protein. Based on these
findings, which of the following additional laboratory tests is most likely to yield a positive result?
Answer Choices: (A) Anti-GBM antibody (B) HBsAg (C) Anti-Ro/SSA antibody (D) c-ANCA (E) p-ANCA
(F) Rheumatoid factor (RF) (G) Anti-Smith antibody (H) Anti-cardiolipin antibody (I) ANA (antinuclear
antibody) (J) Anti-dsDNA antibody
